headline: Stocks bounced Friday after the worst day since April 2025, but a hot jobs report lifted December hike odds to about 73-80%; CPI on Tuesday is the next test.
regime: Hiking regime, volatility easing but elevated: the Fed raised rates in September, and October payrolls of +165k (vs about 65k expected) pushed CME FedWatch odds of a Dec 9 hike to roughly 73-80%. The VIX fell to 25.64 on Friday from 28.18, but the Nasdaq is still in a correction after the Nov 5 AI-regulation selloff. Good economic news can be bad for stocks here.

lean.why: Dow futures are up about 0.6-0.8%, S&P futures +0.3-0.4% and Nasdaq-100 futures flat to -0.3% as Nvidia drops over 4% on its CEO probe. Constellation is up over 4% on earnings. Trade small before CPI.
CPI (Nov 10), CoreWeave (Nov 10), Nebius, Cisco and Applied Materials (Nov 12), PPI (Nov 13) and the Dec 8-9 FOMC all sit ahead. Hike odds near 75% keep yields in focus.

Prices are lower after the Nov 5 drop (semis about 30% off peaks per Schwab), but a hiking Fed and AI data-center regulation talk (Goldman: about 45% of planned US capacity faces possible limits) are real risks.

rates.n: Held Oct 28; next meeting Dec 8-9 (older reading, no new Fed decision since)
CME FedWatch about 73% after the jobs report (Schwab, Nov 6); about 80% (CoinCentral, Nov 9); was 60% Thursday
Freddie Mac survey of Nov 5 (older; next release Thursday Nov 12)

sectors.why: (Nov 4 read, not updated.) Democratic control keeps federal clean-energy support alive. First Solar rose 4.63% on Nov 4.
(Nov 5 read.) Health care fell 2.50% on Nov 5. Friday: UnitedHealth -0.40%, Abbott -3.23%; Moderna +5.27% on a raised revenue outlook.
(Nov 4 read, not updated.) Lockheed -7%, L3Harris -6%. Defense budgets have usually been bipartisan.

Chips bounced Friday after Thursday's SOX drop of more than 12%: AMD +11.04%, Lam +8.23%, Intel +7.71%, Micron +5.12%, Nvidia +2.78%. Nvidia is down over 4% premarket Monday on a board probe of its CEO.
(Nov 5 read.) Financials fell 2.87% on Nov 5. A hot jobs report and higher hike odds help margins but raise credit and growth worries. Bank of America -0.68% Friday.
NVR is up more than 26% premarket after Democrats won Congress; UBS says lower building-material tariffs become likelier. The 10-year at 4.86% and a 7.18% mortgage rate remain headwinds.
Gold fell 0.94% to $4,075 Friday as the dollar rose 0.66% and hike odds jumped.
WTI is about $90.83 (+0.34%) after Wednesday's 8% drop; Brent is just under $100. Occidental reports after the close Monday.
The Russell 2000 rose 0.89% to 2,754.11 Friday after a 4.45% drop Nov 5. Hike odds near 75% are a headwind for borrowers.
(Nov 5 read.) Tesla fell 10.77% and SpaceX 9.05% on Nov 5. No newer sourced reading.
Constellation is up over 4% premarket after a Q3 beat, a raised 2026 EPS guide ($12.50-$12.80) and a 20-year Amazon deal. Power names fell on Nov 5 on data-center regulation fears.
(Nov 4 read, not updated.) GEO -6.7% and CoreCivic -5.2% on the new Congress.

news.head: Nvidia falls over 4% premarket as its board probes CEO Jensen Huang
news.mean: Nvidia's board is investigating whether Huang was a target of a foreign intelligence effort after a media report of a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman. Huang said he was unfaithful and took full responsibility. Nvidia says it has no reason to believe US national-security or company secrets were compromised. Shares fell over 4% premarket; they closed Friday at $186.64 (+2.78%). CoinCentral calls the spy allegation unproven.
react: Chips bounced 5-11% Friday; sympathy move unclear
news.hist: Rule of thumb: headline risk about a mega-cap CEO can swing the Nasdaq-100 even when the company's business is unchanged.
news.today: Details are unverified media reports; opening-bell swings can reverse. Size small.
news.later: A governance story is different from an earnings miss; investors usually wait for facts on whether operations or customers are affected.

news.head: Constellation Energy jumps over 4% on Q3 beat and raised 2026 guidance
news.mean: Adjusted EPS was $5.06 vs $3.89 expected and revenue $9.55B vs $9.35B. 2026 adjusted operating EPS guidance is $12.50-$12.80 vs $12.22 expected, raised at the midpoint for the second time this year. It is buying a 609 MW Rhode Island plant from Shell for $715M, has a 690 MW 20-year Amazon deal and a conditional DOE loan guarantee of up to $5B.
react: Beat and raise, over 4% up premarket
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a beat-and-raise helps the group, but power names were sold on Nov 5 on regulation fears, so the read-through may fade.
news.today: Watch whether the premarket gain holds at the open; options had implied about an 8% move.
news.later: The company is tying growth to long-term contracts with hyperscalers; investors would weigh that against regulatory risk.

news.head: October CPI on Tuesday is the last inflation read before the Dec 8-9 FOMC
news.mean: Consensus is headline +0.3% m/m (prior +0.6%) and core +0.2% (prior +0.3%); the Cleveland Fed nowcast is 0.24% headline and 0.21% core. The report notes the BLS could not collect October 2025 prices, so most 12-month changes will not be published. Schwab lists CPI at 8:30 a.m. ET on Nov 10.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a core number above consensus tends to push yields up and growth stocks down; a cooler print does the opposite.
news.today: Expect a wide range around 8:30 ET; the bond market closes Wednesday for Veterans Day.
news.later: One CPI report rarely changes the long-term picture; the trend over several months matters more for rates.

news.head: October payrolls +165k vs about 65k expected; unemployment 4.1%
news.mean: Payrolls rose 165,000 (consensus cited at 59k-70k), unemployment was 4.1% vs 4.2% expected, and wages rose 0.4% m/m vs 0.3%. August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000, and the three-month average is 137,000.
react: Mixed: margins up, growth outlook better
Gold fell 0.94% as the dollar rose
news.hist: Rule of thumb: strong jobs data in a hiking regime lifts rate expectations, which usually helps the dollar and pressures gold and housing.
news.today: The data is old news by Monday; focus has shifted to CPI.
news.later: The Fed has raised once this cycle, and another hike is now the market's base case; investors weigh rate risk in rate-sensitive holdings.

news.head: December hike odds jump to about 73-80% after the jobs report
news.mean: CME FedWatch put the Dec 9 hike odds at about 73% after payrolls, up from 60% on Thursday (Schwab); CoinCentral cites about 80% on Monday. Reuters via Stock Titan said above 65%. The next FOMC meeting is Dec 8-9.
react: Higher hike odds weigh on bonds
news.hist: Rule of thumb: hike odds are a market estimate that can swing several points on one data release.
news.today: Sources differ on the exact odds (about 73% to 80%), so use a range.
news.later: Rate-sensitive sectors tend to lag while odds are rising; banks can benefit from higher rates.

news.head: Stocks bounce Friday: S&P 500 +0.31%, Nasdaq +1.09%, Dow -0.46%
news.mean: The S&P 500 closed at 7,376.86, the Nasdaq at 24,579.42 and the Dow at 51,285.73, ending a rough week (S&P about -2.7%, Nasdaq about -3.4% per CNBC via Stock Titan). The VIX fell 9% to 25.64. Monday futures: Dow +0.6%, S&P +0.35%, Nasdaq-100 -0.3%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: after a big one-day drop, a partial bounce is common, but it does not by itself mark a low.
news.today: Futures are mixed, so the open depends on Nvidia and CPI positioning.
news.later: Corrections that start from a policy scare are hard to time; staged buying limits timing risk.

news.head: Chips rebound Friday: AMD +11%, Lam Research +8% on a $25B buyback, Intel +7.7%
news.mean: After Thursday's drop (SOX more than 12%, Nvidia -9.26%, AMD -17.26%), AMD rose 11.04%, Lam Research 8.23% after a $25B buyback, Intel 7.71%, Marvell 5.73%, Qualcomm 5.52%, Micron 5.12%, Arm 4.74% and Nvidia 2.78%. Schwab says semis are about 30% below their peaks.
react: Small bounce, now a probe headline
news.hist: Rule of thumb: large one-day rebounds after a crash are common but often retest the lows.
news.today: Chip volatility is extreme; Applied Materials and Cisco report Nov 12.
news.later: Investors would separate buyback-supported companies from those depending on data-center capex.

news.head: Democrats win Congress; AI data-center rules and tariff relief are the market's two read-throughs
news.mean: Investors fear rules on AI data centers; Goldman estimates about 45% of planned US data-center capacity faces possible restrictions (Yahoo). On the other side, homebuilders rallied (NVR up more than 26% premarket) because UBS says Democratic control could improve the odds of lower tariffs on building materials.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: policy surprises are often priced fast, then re-priced as the details emerge.
news.today: State-level data-center headlines can move the group in minutes.
news.later: Divided government usually slows big new laws; permits and power rules are the practical risk.

news.head: Earnings movers: Gogo +72%, Karman +42%, Firefly +37%, JFrog +35%; DraftKings -21%, Opendoor -22%
news.mean: Gogo rose 71.52% after the FCC renewed its licenses through 2036. Karman gained 42.13% on Q3 revenue +66% to $202M. Firefly rose 36.80% on a $1.3B+ engine deal with AST SpaceMobile. JFrog rose 35.33%. Airbnb +11.67% and Cloudflare +9.91%. Decliners: iRhythm -30.70%, Opendoor -21.79%, DraftKings -21.30%, Atlassian -16.15%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: post-earnings gaps in small caps often extend or reverse in the next few sessions; no pattern is reliable.
news.today: Names that gapped 30%+ Friday are high risk for fade or follow-through.
news.later: Single-quarter moves matter less than whether guidance changes the multi-year story.

news.head: This week: CEG, Rocket Lab, Occidental (Mon); CPI, CoreWeave (Tue); Nebius, Cisco, Applied Materials (Thu); PPI (Fri)
news.mean: Schwab lists CEG and Barrick Monday morning and Occidental and Rocket Lab Monday afternoon; CPI plus CoreWeave and Rigetti on Tuesday; existing home sales, Brookfield, Nebius, Cisco and Applied Materials Thursday; PPI Friday. CoreWeave consensus revenue is about $3.5B (+159% y/y).
react: AI and space names with big implied moves
news.hist: Rule of thumb: earnings weeks right after a selloff often carry larger-than-average moves for the most-exposed names.
news.today: Check implied moves before sizing; several carry 13-21% options-implied moves.
news.later: Investors might wait for guidance commentary rather than react to the first print.

news.head: Oil steady near $91: WTI $90.83 (+0.34%), Brent below $100
news.mean: WTI December futures closed at $90.83 (+0.34%) Friday; Schwab had WTI at $91.10 at the open. The prior Thursday close was WTI $90.52 and Brent $98.29 after Wednesday's drop of more than 8% (Zacks).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: oil above $90 keeps headline inflation elevated.
news.later: Energy exposure has been volatile; investors might note the 8% one-day drop on Nov 4.

news.head: Gold slips to $4,075 (-0.94%) as the dollar rises 0.66%
news.mean: Gold futures closed at $4,074.90, down 0.94%; Schwab had spot at $4,060.70 (-1.31%) at the open. The dollar index was 102.22 (+0.66%) and the 10-year yield 4.86%.
react: Pressure from the dollar and yields
news.hist: Rule of thumb: gold often falls when the dollar and real yields rise together.
news.today: Watch CPI: a hot core number can push gold lower again.
news.later: Gold is a long-term hedge; investors weigh it against rising real yields.

calendar.t: Constellation (reported), Rocket Lab and Occidental earnings
calendar.usual: CEG is up over 4% premarket; Rocket Lab options imply about 15%. Tests the data-center power and space themes.

calendar.t: October CPI (8:30 ET); CoreWeave after the close
calendar.usual: Consensus headline +0.3%, core +0.2%. The key input to December's hike; core matters more than the headline.

calendar.t: Veterans Day: bond market closed, stocks open
calendar.usual: Thin Treasury trading; no major US data.

calendar.t: Freddie Mac mortgage rates; Nebius, Cisco, Applied Materials earnings
calendar.usual: AI infrastructure read-through; the last survey was 7.18%.
Follows CPI; can move yields if it surprises.
Corporate buybacks often support stocks after blackout periods end.

out: Relief; focus moves to Nebius and Cisco

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
